Maria (CS): quick ops pulse for AcmeCorp onboarding — 24h error break down and top failpoints. flagging renewal risk if we don't stabilize. TL;DR: 5xx spikes + timeouts + a noisy rate-limit pattern.

HealthBot: [ALERT] AcmeCorp - error rate exceeded threshold (2.5%) at 2026-03-18T03:20Z :warning:

Tom (SRE): Seen it. 5xx spike at ~03:20-03:45 UTC, one of the GPU workers hit repeated OOMs and churned. Impact concentrated on session-heavy routes.

Viktor (Eng): looking at traces now — root cause looks like a KV cache thrash + large prompt bursts causing sequence length blowup for some requests. we'll repro locally.

Evan (AE): customer notes: onboarding scripts send ~30 requests/sec during import, and they use our long-context playground heavily. they mentioned latency regressed yesterday. Renewal call scheduled next week — want to avoid surprises.

Maria (CS): Action items: 1) SRE contain 5xx and roll to a lower-memory pool if needed. 2) Eng to add input-size guardrails and better metrics for seq-length by customer. 3) I'll brief AE on mitigation steps for renewal.

Tom (SRE): Quick breakdown (24h window):
- 5xx: 1.9% overall, but Acme onboarding namespace = 6.7% (spike period included)
- timeouts: 0.8% (mostly websocket timeouts during heavy imports)
- rate-limits: bursts causing 429s at client-level: 0.5% (traffic pattern: short spikes)

Top failing endpoints (ranked by Acme impact):
1) /api/v1/session/generate — 412 failures, 62% are 5xx (worker OOM & GPU preemption)
2) /ws/stream/resp — 178 failures, mostly timeouts when payload > 64k tokens
3) /api/v1/embeddings/batch — 94 failures, many 429s from client-side burst (client_key=acme-import)
4) /api/v1/rewrite — 44 failures, intermittent 5xx in fallback path

Tom (SRE): Example logs from worker-12 during spike:
```
[2026-03-18T03:23:12Z] ERROR worker-12: OOM while allocating 1.2G for attention_kv
[2026-03-18T03:23:12Z] WARN router: retrying request id=abc123 after worker crash
[2026-03-18T03:23:13Z] ERROR router: all workers busy -> 502 response to client id=abc123
```

Viktor (Eng): Short-term mitigations I can push today: 1) knob to cap sequence length per-request for preset "onboarding" route, 2) autoscale temp to add more workers for that pool, 3) fallback to a smaller model variant for heavy sessions. I'll open PR for 1 & 3.

Maria (CS): Can SRE perform a transient routing rule to move Acme traffic to dedicated low-latency pool while Eng lands the guardrails? That'd reduce immediate noise for the renewal call.

Tom (SRE): Yes — I'll create a routing override for the next 24h and monitor. If OOMs persist we'll shift to the dedicated low-mem pool and throttle large seqs.

Evan (AE): I'll tell Acme to pause import window and retry with staged batches. Also offering a 1:1 enablement session on best-practice request shapes. Lets coordinate time after we stabilize. :+1:

HealthBot: [INCIDENT] Incident created: #INC-2026-4823 assigned to SRE. Links: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-4823

Maria (CS): Good. please add the spike charts to the incident and drop a short note for the renewal pack. I'll update the account health dashboard with adjusted risk = "elevated" until next check-in.

Viktor (Eng): PR opened for seq cap + model fallback: https://github.com/redwood/serve/pull/8123 — includes a metric tagged by customer_id so we can track seq-length by tenant.

Tom (SRE): Monitoring plan: watch 5xx rate, avg seq-length, and worker OOMs. I'll post a 6hr update in this thread.

Maria (CS): Thanks team — we'll reconvene after the 6hr check. Evan, I'll loop you into the incident notes for the renewal talking points. :eyes:
